newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper stocks seen up by 3,000-10,000T - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stocks seen up by 3,000-10,000T - trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks are seen rising by between 3,000 to 10,000 tonnes with the volume of red metal reaching Singapore expected to rise further over the next few weeks, traders said on Tuesday.
LME aluminium stocks are seen slipping by 1,000-4,000 tonnes when the LME report comes out later on Tuesday, they said.
"It (copper) will be up by 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes," the general manager of a European metals desk said, adding the increase was not seen duplicating the sharp rise last Friday.
Copper stocks rose by an unexpectedly steep 15,325 tonnes in Friday's LME report.
"I feel copper should only be 3,000-5,000 tonnes up," the managing director of a Japanese trading house added.

Dealers said the amount of material arriving in Singapore is likely to rise further, although the long Chinese Lunar New Year holiday last week will trim the amount being reported in the LME stocks report.

"The LME warehouse here has been shut since Friday. Very little will probably come on the report as a result," one trader said. "There has been a lot of material coming here and we'll probably see more material come in."
Most of the copper reaching Singapore is arriving from Chile with some from Europe, the traders said.
On Friday, the amount of copper in the LME's Singapore warehouse climbed to 52,675 tonnes after reaching a year low of just under 2,000 tonnes at the beginning of October, 1996.
Copper prices were little changed to slightly higher in lethargic post-holiday trade in the Far East, traders here said.
Three-month copper prices were quoted by regional dealers at 0200 GMT at around US$2,237/42 a tonne against the late trade in London yesterday of $2,235 a tonne.
Aluminium prices were seen at about $1,581/85 a tonne compared to the late quote in London on Monday of $1,580 a tonne, the dealers said.
